_comment: Structure pieces that fill a chest through generateStructureChestContents but never ask Forge for a
loot table: they pass their own compile-time WeightedRandomChestContent[] and their own roll count.
The count is drawn from the chunk-populate Random. That Random IS position-seeded -- RWG reseeds it from
(worldSeed, cx, cz) immediately before the structure generators run -- so these chests are deterministic
today. What they are not is CHEAP to compute: reaching the count means replaying the populate prologue
(the PopulateChunkEvent.Pre handlers, then the mineshaft and stronghold generators) for the chunk, which
the worldless stage-0 prefilter does not do.
F10 therefore redraws the count from the chest's own position fork instead, over the range the mod itself
uses. Same distribution, same pool, no dependence on anything but the chest's position -- so the prefilter
can predict it with the same two lines the fix runs.
min and max are INCLUSIVE and are read from the mod's bytecode, not inferred from samples. field is the
static array the piece passes. Both jars load this file; they must agree, and the acceptance test is a
generateStructureChestContents at all -- it places the chest and writes slots directly through
TileEntityChest.setInventorySlotContents -- so no hook sees it and neither jar can touch it.
